newsitem.title: UK: Seven, eight-year gilts sought on UK gilt repo mkt.
newsitem.headline: Seven, eight-year gilts sought on UK gilt repo mkt.

text.p: Seven and eight-year gilts remained in good demand on the UK gilt repo market on Friday, while overnight cash had a volatile day as a one billion stg shortage was not fully covered.
The 6.75 percent gilts due 2004 were bid at around 5.45 for two weeks but activity was moderate, while the 8.0s of 2003 were quoted at 5.20 and 5.30 overnight and 5.45 for the week.
The 7.0s of 2001 and 6.0s of 1999 were fairly tight earlier in the day. "Towards the end of the day they freed up a little bit and are not so tight now," one trader said.
General collateral business was fairly subdued.
"GC was all over the place towards the end of the day because of the heavy shortage in the cash up until late assistance," a trader said.
One-month GC was quoted at 5.70 65, two months at 5.67 64 and three months at 5.66 62.
The Bank of England provided assistance totalling 857 million stg after forecasting a shortage of one billion.
The latest screen rates for overnight cash were around 5-13/16 3/4 but traders said it had ended around two percent.

Looking ahead to next week, analysts at Union Discount said the success of Wednesday's repo tender and the behaviour of money market rates in general would depend in part on sentiment ahead of the September 23 monetary meeting.

"Should market optimism over a rate cut revive over the coming week (which we doubt), this would result in a disappointing allocation in the gilt repo and tend to push the overnight rate higher," they wrote in their weekly economic review.
